- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.6) and recent price action is trending up — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (e.g., <0.3) — model fails to account for downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction after sharp price increases.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is rising but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment and forecasts downward — reverse direction if sentiment >0.5 and price > recent high.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3–0.7), model tends to smooth out extremes — use sentiment as a multiplier (e.g., +10% if sentiment >0.7, -10% if <0.3) to adjust forecast mean.
